units.summary: Adds a test that evicts a series via CompactSelectedSeries, forces a WAL checkpoint, and asserts the evicted series' record is still in the checkpoint. It is a new test only, so it cannot change production behavior.
units.headline: New test: evicted selected series stays in WAL checkpoint
units.reason: New test-only addition that covers the walExpiry checkpoint path and does not alter production code.

units.summary: Generalizes the stale-only head truncation into a shared helper that takes an eviction predicate and returns the evicted count. The early-return guard changes from MinTime >= maxt to MinTime > maxt, so a single-timestamp head is now evicted. Tombstones are still logged to the WAL for the deleted refs.
units.headline: truncateSeries takes eviction predicate, now inclusive of MinTime == maxt
units.reason: The boundary condition changed and the function now drives eviction of non-stale series, which affects head data and WAL tombstones.
focus: Callers that relied on truncation being skipped when MinTime == maxt (CompactStaleHead path)
WAL tombstones logged only for refs actually deleted, and replay ignoring them correctly
WaitForPendingReadersInTimeRange(MinTime, maxt) is still sufficient for the inclusive bound

units.summary: Renames gcStaleSeries to gcSeries and takes an eviction predicate. numStaleSeries is now decremented only by the count of deleted series that were actually stale, instead of by every deleted series. This keeps the stale counter correct when non-stale series are evicted.
units.headline: gcSeries decrements numStaleSeries only for stale evicted series
units.reason: The metric and counter accounting changed, and eviction now covers non-stale series, which affects head state.
risk_signals: uint64 subtraction could underflow if counts drift
focus: numStaleSeries stays consistent with the series actually stale at deletion time
numSeries and seriesRemoved metrics still use the full deleted count

units.summary: The hardcoded stale-NaN check is replaced by a caller-supplied shouldEvict predicate. The function now also counts deleted series that were stale, via isStaleSeries, and returns that count. The stale-specific behavior moves to the callers' predicates.
units.headline: stripeSeries gcSeries uses pluggable predicate and counts stale deletions
units.reason: The core series deletion condition is now supplied by the caller, so what gets evicted from the head depends on each predicate.
risk_signals: deletion criteria moved to a callback
concurrency (runs under series locks in iterForDeletion)
focus: The predicate runs under the series lock and must not take other locks
Every caller's predicate keeps the OOO and appendID safety checks that protect against data loss
isStaleSeries is evaluated on the same state that shouldEvict saw
